title: Factory hardening follow-up: guard gaps, check override, trivial gate
request: Doug said yes to the factory hardening follow-up: (1) a trivial task must still be blocked by a recorded REJECT or CHANGES review; (2) refuse the check -- <cmd> override for every check; (3) close the push-to-a-protected-branch gap inside $( ), backticks, <( ), >( ), a subshell and a glued redirect; (4) stop the F check constructor crash; (5) a fail-closed cap on deep nesting in the guard; (6) README wording fixes plus the smoke-test result; (7) two test pins. Doug also confirmed by hand on 2026-11-04 that the hook ask prompted him in Auto mode, even when an allow rule matched.

criteria.text: F check <id> constructor, __proto__ and toString end with a plain No command for check error (exit 1): no TypeError, and no check record is written. Test first (RED on the old code).

F check <id> <name> -- <cmd> is refused for EVERY name (required, configured, or unknown): nothing runs and no record is written. The old test that expected a configured, not-required check to accept the override is replaced by its inverse. That is a deliberate decision by Doug (follow-up yes), not a weakened test. Test first.

A --trivial task whose latest code review is CHANGES or REJECT is NOT ready. A trivial task with an APPROVE, or with no review at all, still passes. Test first. factory/PIPELINE.md (two places) and the README line say so.

The guard blocks a push to a protected branch inside $( ), backticks, <( ), >( ), a no-space subshell and with a redirect glued to the branch word. Controls stay true: a quoted ) before main is still blocked, and a feature-branch push inside $( ) is still allowed. Tests first: they fail on the old guard (I saw the old guard allow all six).

A command that nests more than 64 levels deep is BLOCKED by the guard (fail closed) with a plain reason, in well under a second. A command nested 60 deep is still checked normally. Real timings before and after are saved (before: 100 deep 216 ms, 250 deep 1039 ms, 400 deep 4270 ms).

Two test pins: (a) a test that fails if the visited-set key stopped including the depth, and (b) a deeper timing test with a generous bound. Each is shown to fail when the thing it pins is broken (mutation run).

factory/README.md: the three wording fixes (the quoted-heredoc form needs a second EOF line; the quote-nesting limit also holds for a single-quoted word with a double quote; deep-nest timings vary by machine), the smoke-test result (dated 2026-11-04: Doug saw a prompt for both tests, so the hook ask prompted in Auto mode and beat an allow rule), and every known-limit line this task fixes is rewritten. Nothing else in the README changes meaning.

The guard was developed on a COPY and installed in one step: the installed factory/hooks/guard.mjs is byte-identical (sha256) to the copy that passed the specs, and node --check passes on it. The hook was never left in a broken state.

All required repo checks and the factory-specs check pass on the final commit, and a fresh independent reviewer approves it. Left alone and reported: git -C and git -c push or commit forms, the secret scan skip for those forms, the other documented limits.

reviews.summary: Independent PLAN review: CHANGES, all points accepted in plan v2. The first push fix would have opened a hole (git push 2>/dev/null on main) and missed five forms; the cap must also bound width; the work copy needs .claude, .github and tools; keep the two specific override refusals.

Fresh reviewer: CHANGES. (1) REGRESSION, verified: a bare 'push' or 'push <remote>' on a protected branch, inside $( ) or backticks or an array subscript, with text glued after the closer, was blocked by the old guard and is allowed now. (2) The paren floor in parenDepth has no test. (3) New false positives: a protected name in ( ) [ ] { } after a push word in a commit message or PR body. (4) The cap does not bound run time for a very large body. (5) parenDepth counts parens inside quotes. (6) Some mutants survive. (7) README says F resolve crashes on a prototype key; it does not. CLI changes A1-A3 reviewed as fine.

history.summary: Read each push two ways (tidy and plain); a block from either wins. Zero regressions against the old guard on 729 curated pushes, 420 spec inputs, 166 normal commands, 374 depth cases and 3 fuzz seeds checked against real bash.

review1-push-regression.resolved: fixed in e6fcced and 68eaf29, verified by test and by corpus

history.summary: Added tests for the paren floor, for a heredoc body not counting toward the cap, for the push with glued text, and for braces and brackets. Six deliberate breakages of the guard are each caught by a test.

review1-test-gaps.resolved: fixed in e6fcced and 68eaf29, verified by test and by corpus

history.summary: Braces and brackets no longer cut the words of a push. Fewer prose false positives with no push missed. The README lists the ones that remain.

review1-false-positives.resolved: fixed in e6fcced and 68eaf29, verified by test and by corpus

history.summary: README: size limit with measured times, parens in quotes, the repair and resolve prototype-key wording checked by running the CLI. The comment on the cap no longer calls the counts cheap.

review1-doc-gaps.resolved: fixed in e6fcced and 68eaf29, verified by test and by corpus
